patch_description: The current ansatz uses fixed CZ gates for entanglement, meaning the entangling structure is non-trainable and identical across all layers. This wastes representational capacity: the single-qubit rotations must compensate for a fixed, potentially mismatched entangling pattern. I replace the fixed CZ gates with parametrized CRZ gates that share a single learnable parameter per repetition ("crz_ent"), allowing the model to learn the strength of entanglement (from ~0 essentially identity to full CZ-like behavior) while adding only one extra parameter per block repetition (6 total across the circuit, from 162 to 168 params). This is a low-risk, low-parameter-cost change that gives the optimizer control over entanglement strength, which can help match the actual correlation structure of the data, potentially improving accuracy while keeping the train-test gap and parameter efficiency good.
